result.title: Designing Textual Interfaces To Enhance Llm Reasoning On Audio-Visual Question Answering
result.summary: Automatic prompt optimization (APO) has shown strong effectiveness for text-based LLMs and LLM systems, but its application to audio-visual understanding systems requires suitable textual interfaces through which multimodal reasoning can be exposed to text-based optimizers. We investigate how the design of textual interfaces affects prompt optimization for multimodal reasoning, on the audio-visual question answering task. We compare three interface designs, including a direct inference system consisting of a single omni-modal large language model (OmniLLM), a captioner-reasoner system, and an agentic architecture in which a primary agent orchestrates subagent OmniLLMs. Experiments with Qwen3-Omni and Gemini show that direct prompt optimization provides model-dependent gains; the captioner-reasoner system and the agentic system expose more interpretable optimization interfaces but are harder to optimize, where error analysis of cases affected by optimization is conducted. Our study highlights textual interface design as an important factor in making prompt optimization effective for omni-modal reasoning systems. Our implementation details are specified in GitHub repo.

AI.brief_summary: 在音频-视觉问答任务上比较三种文本接口设计（单一 OmniLLM 直接推理、captioner-reasoner 两段式、主智能体编排子 OmniLLM 的 agentic 架构）对自动提示优化效果的影响，并对受优化影响的案例做错误分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文把多模态推理外化为可被文本优化器操作的接口，其「直接推理 vs 先描述再推理」的对比可能与潜状态中视觉证据是否被保留、caption 旁路导致的信息坍缩有可供核查的联系，但未涉及 latent 状态本身。
